Topic: Mastering the Putnam: Strategy & Aesthetic Problem Solving

Target audience: Undergraduate students with a strong background in Calculus and Linear Algebra

Section: section_1 — The Putnam Mindset: Beyond Computational Drills

Lecture lines:
Putnam problems test structural insight, not speed.
Adopt the Discovery Cycle: Observe, Conjecture, Prove.
Visualize logical paths like a detective's map.
Identify symmetry, not just brute-force calculation.
[Asset: Squirrel_Symmetry_Visualization] Focus on geometric patterns.

Planned animations:
Display title "The Putnam Mindset" in #FFFFFF.
Fade in sub-header "Beyond Computational Drills" in #AAAAAA.
Highlight "Mindset" in #FFD700.

Section: section_2 — Prerequisite Mastery: The Toolkit

Lecture lines:
Master the 'Big Three' foundational pillars.
Extremal Principle, Invariants, and Parity/Coloring arguments.
Invariants identify what remains unchanged during transformation.
Parity tests if a path is possible.
[Asset: Invariant_Tiling_Animation] Area remains constant.

Planned animations:
Display title "Prerequisite Mastery" in #FFFFFF.
Show icons of algebra, combinatorics, and geometry in #4169E1.
Fade in "The Toolkit" text in #FFFFFF.

Section: section_3 — Strategy: Thinking in Extremes

Lecture lines:
Use the Extremal Principle for optimization.
Assume an extreme element forces a contradiction.
Highlights peaks to anchor proofs by induction.
Simpler boundaries aid complex sensor equations.
[Asset: Robotic_Arm_Extremal_Graph] Finding optimal points.

Planned animations:
Display title "Thinking in Extremes" in #FFFFFF.
Show two opposite extremes (infinity/zero) on a number line in #FF4500.
Animate movement between these poles.

Section: section_4 — Applying the 'Small Case' Heuristic

Lecture lines:
Reduction bridges intuition and rigorous formalization.
If n is complex, test n equals one.
Sequence visualizers show patterns from low-level data.
Map complex cases to manageable smaller ones.
[Asset: Explorer_Bridge_Small_Case] Testing strength weights.

Planned animations:
Display title "The 'Small Case' Heuristic" in #FFFFFF.
Show simple shapes representing n=1, 2, 3 in #32CD32.
Transition through these cases procedurally.

Section: section_5 — Conclusion: The Final Synthesis

Lecture lines:
Simplify, Explore Invariants, Apply Extremes, Prove.
Treat Putnam problems as puzzles, not tests.
Integrate your logic engine for synthesis.

Planned animations:
Display title "The Final Synthesis" in #FFFFFF.
Show the pieces of the problem coming together in #9370DB.
Animate the completed picture in #FFFFFF.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        lecture_lines = [

            "If n is complex, test n equals one.",
            "Sequence visualizers show patterns from low-level data.",
            "Map complex cases to manageable smaller ones.",
            "Testing strength weights."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Applying the 'Small Case' Heuristic", lecture_lines)

        self.wait(1)

        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        dot1 = Dot(color="#32CD32").scale(2)
        self.place_at_grid(dot1, 'B2')
        self.play(FadeIn(dot1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        dot2 = Dot(color="#FFD700").scale(2)
        dot3 = Dot(color="#FFD700").scale(2)
        self.place_at_grid(dot2, 'B3')
        self.place_at_grid(dot3, 'B4')
        self.play(FadeIn(dot2), FadeIn(dot3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF6347"))
        line = Line(start=self.grid['B2'], end=self.grid['B4'], color="#FF6347")
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        # Using placeholder for Asset: Explorer_Bridge_Small_Case
        explorer = Square(color="#FFFFFF", fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(explorer, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(explorer))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
